audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart read 'Skill' on all seven rows while the content layer and the packet levelChart both give Orianna rows 1-2 and Viktor rows 4-5 and 2+ items. Two layers rendered two different answers.
audit.why: Packet levelChart and content win[] agree, and the kit supports it: pre-3 Viktor has only Siphon Power (600 range, 9s at rank 1) while Orianna's Q is 815 range on 7s; after the Hextech Ray augment his clear and poke out-range her.
audit.corrected: Full-layer phases[0].side/[1].side set to Orianna, phases[3].side and phases[6].side set to Viktor, whys rewritten to match, ratings adjusted. Content win[] already held the correct tokens so no content edit was required.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text named a non-existent ability ('Death Ray', 'Chaos Storm') and claimed his R silences and is channelled.
audit.why: Riot's kit text gives E = Hextech Ray and R = Arcane Storm; the R conjures a storm that interrupts enemy channels and is redirected by Viktor, it does not silence and he is not locked in a channel.
audit.corrected: Real names used throughout; the R described as a redirectable zone that interrupts channels; Orianna R cooldown 110/95/80 stated where it makes advice concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: No ability-by-ability interaction stated, and the auto-attack reset on Siphon Power was never mentioned.
audit.why: Siphon Power grants a shield and empowers his next basic attack (auto reset) — the wind-up, not the cast, is the tell that his trade has started. Gravity Field only stuns after you linger inside it, so stepping out of the ring removes the lock entirely. Both his Q (600) and E (525) are shorter than Orianna's Q (815) and E (1095).
audit.corrected: Cooldowns field now carries Gravity Field 17s->13s, Hextech Ray 12s->8s and Orianna R 110s; the do's bullet keys trading to his 9s Siphon Power; the don'ts bullet keys the ball position to his 600/525 ranges.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: It is the field that holds real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Gravity Field 17/16/15/14/13, Hextech Ray 12/11/10/9/8, Command: Shockwave 110/95/80 stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood pasted verbatim; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad pasted verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: Body did not match the promised title.
audit.corrected: Both replaced with content that answers their own titles.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.mid claimed protect-ball 'doubles every gank' (lint UNSUPPORTED_MAGNITUDE).
audit.why: No number in the kit supports 'doubles'.
audit.corrected: Replaced with what the ball actually delivers: a shield, the movement speed field, and the R riding along.

edits.before: Ball on the wave, autos on his face — your passive-stacked autos win level 1 against almost every mid. Place, don't throw.
edits.after: Ball on the wave, autos on his face — Siphon Power is 600 range on 9s, so you out-trade him before he has an answer.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Orianna

edits.before: Q-W online: the classic chunk combo. Trade it on his last-hits and keep the ball where his approach must cross it.
edits.after: Q-W online and still yours: chunk him on his last-hits while Hextech Ray is unlearned and his only trade is a 9s Q.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Viktor

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q-W every wave contact now. The Dissonance field controls every step he takes near the ball.
edits.after: Augmented Hextech Ray out-clears and out-pokes you here — hold the ball home-side, farm safe, and play for level 6.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Viktor

edits.before: Late Ori is the teamfight: protect-ball on your diver, shockwave their clump, and dissonance the choke they retreat through.
edits.after: A finished Viktor out-ranges and out-DPSes you in sustained fights — your value is one Shockwave from max range, not a duel.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E Command: Protect has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Gravity Field (W): 17s at rank 1, 13s at rank 5 — it only stuns if you linger, so walk out of the ring and his all-in has no lock. - Hextech Ray (E): 12s at rank 1 down to 8s — his clear and his poke both sit on it, so step up the moment it is spent. - Your R at 110s is for his commit, not a wave.

edits.before: From Luden's you run rivers: shove the wave, hover the ball at the choke, and Shockwave the first clump that contests. Protect-ball on your jungler doubles every gank.
edits.after: From Luden's you run rivers: shove, hover the ball at the choke, and Shockwave the first clump that contests. Protect-ball carries a shield, the speed field and your R into your jungler's gank.

edits.before: The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Siphon Power is 600 range and Hextech Ray 525 — a ball parked on his last-hit spot taxes him for standing where he must stand.

edits.before: Ball on his farm path, Q-W the last-hit contact, auto-weave once, and recall the ball — three-second trades his combo math can't answer.
edits.after: Your Q is 7s at rank 1 dropping to 3s at rank 5, cheaper than his 9s Siphon Power — chunk him on every minion he steps up for, then recall the ball.

edits.before: Viktor spends Gravity Field early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Your passive damage grows on repeat hits — weave an auto between Q and W, never cast and walk.

edits.before: That is Viktor’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Ball-less, his 600-range Q and 525 E both out-reach you.

edits.before: Poking with the ball stranded at max range when his engage is up — an Orianna without her ball is a Doran's Ring with legs.
edits.after: Your R is 110s at rank 1 — spending it on minions leaves the next objective fight without the one button that decides it.

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Viktor wins by banking Hex Fragments, augmenting Hextech Ray, and out-clearing you until the wave never reaches you.

edits.before: If Viktor gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Gravity Field extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q-W clears and stay relevant through Shockwave threat.
edits.after: A kill funds Hex Fragments and an early augment, so give the Gravity Field ring extra room and farm with Q-W from behind your minions. Two kills: stop stepping inside 600 range at all and hold R for the fight.

edits.before: Carry through the ball — no champion controls teamfight space like Orianna; one Shockwave on three is a won game, and you decide when it happens.
edits.after: Carry through the ball — protect-ball on your engage shields him and delivers your R, so one Shockwave drags his backline out of the Arcane Storm.

edits.before: Your range and ball beat him before his Death Ray is leveled - level 1 yours.
edits.after: Your range and ball beat him before his Hextech Ray is leveled - level 1 yours.

edits.before: His Death Ray comes online at 3 and the poke war levels off.
edits.after: His Hextech Ray comes online at 3 and the poke war levels off.

edits.before: Augmented Death Ray out-clears and out-pokes you through 4-5 - his favour.
edits.after: Augmented Hextech Ray out-clears and out-pokes you through 4-5 - his favour.

edits.before: Everything hinges on his augmented Death Ray (E). Before he upgrades it you win trades - land ball on him and pull back through him while his laser is still a single line. Once he augments E it splits and out-clears you, so this window flips to him; shove before that and freeze him off the upgrade timing.
edits.after: Everything hinges on his augmented Hextech Ray (E). Before he upgrades it you win trades - land ball on him and pull it back through him while the laser is still one line on a 12s cooldown. Once augmented it explodes in its wake and out-clears you, so shove before that and deny him the fragments.

edits.before: Both ults are up and the fight is even. His Chaos Storm (R) is a moving zone that silences and pokes; your Shockwave is burst engage. Neither of you gets a clean solo kill through the other's shield and E, so trade cooldowns rather than committing.
edits.after: Both ults are up and the fight is even. His Arcane Storm (R) is a moving zone he redirects, and it interrupts channels; your Shockwave is burst engage on a 110s cooldown at rank 1. Neither of you kills through the other's shield, so trade cooldowns instead.

edits.before: This is his half of the game. A completed Viktor with augmented E, W stun-zone and Chaos Storm out-DPSes and out-ranges you in extended fights. Play your Shockwave as a pick tool from max range, never a duel, and rely on your team to punish him while he channels R.
edits.after: This is his half of the game. A completed Viktor with augmented Hextech Ray, the Gravity Field stun-zone and Arcane Storm out-DPSes you in extended fights. Play Shockwave as a pick tool from max range, never a duel, and collapse on him once his storm is committed elsewhere.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are yours - your base range and ball harass beat him before his Death Ray is leveled, so step up and chunk him as he last-hits. He has no wave-clear edge yet, so shove and deny his early upgrade fragments.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are yours - your ball reaches 815 where his Siphon Power stops at 600, so step up and chunk him as he last-hits. He has no wave-clear edge yet, so shove and deny his early Hex Fragments.

edits.before: Level 3 evens as his E comes online, and once he augments it at 4-5 the lane tilts to him - the split laser out-clears and out-pokes you, so you lose the shove war. At 6 both ults balance the fight; respect his gravity field and don't duel into his Chaos Storm.
edits.after: Level 3 evens as Hextech Ray comes online, and once he augments it at 4-5 the lane tilts to him - the trailing explosion out-clears you, so you lose the shove war. At 6 both ults balance the fight; step out of Gravity Field rather than fighting inside it, and don't duel into his Arcane Storm.

edits.before: Two-plus items is Viktor's kingdom - augmented E, W stun-zone and Chaos Storm out-range and out-DPS you in any sustained fight. Stop trying to win the sidelane and instead play Shockwave as a long-range pick, letting your team collapse while he is locked into his ult channel.
edits.after: Two-plus items is Viktor's kingdom - augmented Hextech Ray, the Gravity Field stun-zone and Arcane Storm out-range and out-DPS you in any sustained fight. Stop trying to win the sidelane and instead play Shockwave as a long-range pick, collapsing on him once his storm is spent elsewhere.

edits.before: Shove hard before his Death Ray is augmented
edits.after: Shove hard before his Hextech Ray is augmented

edits.before: Augment Death Ray to out-clear and out-poke
edits.after: Augment Hextech Ray to out-clear and out-poke

notes: Full-layer chart disagreed with the content layer on rows 0, 1, 3 and 6 (full said 'Skill' everywhere). The packet levelChart matches the content layer, so the full layer was moved to match; win[] already holds the correct tokens, so no paired content edit exists for those rows. Rows 2, 4 and 5 already agreed and were left alone. Fabricated names 'Death Ray' and 'Chaos Storm' replaced with Hextech Ray and Arcane Storm; the claim that his R silences and that he is 'locked into his ult channel' is contradicted by Riot's text (the storm interrupts channels and is redirected by him) and was removed. Siphon Power's auto-attack reset from missingInteractions is now reflected in the trading advice (his wind-up, not the cast, opens the trade).
